Darryl Moch

DC Statehood Green candidate for At-Large Member of the Council of the District of Columbia · Challenger

Social-justice advocate and community organizer; Chair of the D.C. Statehood Green Party

Darryl Moch is a social-justice advocate who has worked on housing, homelessness and LGBTQ issues, and he chairs the D.C. Statehood Green Party. He was the party's nominee for At-Large Council in 2024 and lost in the general election that November. He is on the DC Board of Elections candidate list as the Statehood Green candidate for At-Large Member of the Council in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Moch stands

Housing
Supports rent control to keep residents from becoming homeless when they can no longer afford rent. Supports expanding programs that help residents who are having trouble paying rent (stated in his 2024 campaign).

Background

  • Chair, D.C. Statehood Green Party (current)
  • D.C. Statehood Green nominee for At-Large DC Council, 2024 (lost general election, Nov. 5, 2024)
  • Reappointed to the Green Party of the United States Finance Committee, May 2026
  • Longtime social-justice advocate on housing, homelessness and LGBTQ issues
  • Described as a reverend and community organizer (2024 coverage)
